chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It was narrated to me by Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Aban ibn Uthman from Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
One who satisfies the hunger of four Muslims, [the reward for him] is equal to freeing a slave from the progeny of Ismail (peace be upon him).

key_terms.ع: Abbreviation for 'Alayhi al-Salam (peace be upon him)
key_terms.مُحَرَّرَهً: A freed slave (female form used here for the reward/concept)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for feeding four Muslims until they are satisfied?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the immense spiritual merit of satisfying four Muslims, equating it to freeing a slave from the progeny of Prophet Ismail (AS), a lineage deeply revered in Islamic tradition for its role in establishing the Kaaba. This comparison highlights the high status of sustenance as an act of worship, linking physical nourishment to the liberation of the soul from worldly constraints, a theme central to Shia ethical teachings on social responsibility and charity.
